Episode 36 of @RuntimeArguments is live at RuntimeArguments.fm: "Now Let's Talk About Leaning the Ladder". It sounds like a productivity episode. It isn't. Wolf @YesJustWolf argues the scarce resource was never time — everyone gets the same clock — it's attention, and where you point it. Jim @jammcq makes the case for saying no: ripgrep, fd, and Helix are noise against an attention budget he'd rather spend on Postgres, TypeScript, and a work-life balance Wolf openly envies. Wolf's answer: success is a multi-dimensional span, not a point, and you're both inside it — you just landed at different spots because you weigh switching cost differently. Also: bit rot isn't decay, it's the world moving while your code stands still; a test is a definition of done that checks itself; don't fall in love with your answer (or your Subaru). Plus Wolf confesses to talking too much, and Jim has a fix. Listeners, hold him to it.

As always, we want to know what you think:
